title: I Ran for Mayor Against a Dog

lines.t: In this town, the Mayor is a dog. And in seven days, I'm running against him.
His name is Biscuit. He has won five elections in a row. He can't even read.
The rule: every vote costs one dollar. Vote as many times as you want.
Day one. I put my poster on every house in town. Biscuit peed on all of them.
Day two. I promised free pizza every Friday. The crowd cheered. Then Biscuit rolled over. They cheered louder.
Day three. I kissed a baby. Then Biscuit gave the baby a big lick. The baby's whole family voted Biscuit.
Day four. My best friend Benny sold cookies for me. He made three hundred dollars. Three hundred votes!
Day five. Biscuit got a TV ad. It was just him sleeping. Everybody loved it.
Day six. The big debate. I talked about new roads, a park, and fixing the school roof.
Biscuit sat. Then he gave the host his paw. Standing ovation.
Election night. The whole town on the square. The big screen counting every dollar.
Me: three hundred and twelve. Biscuit: three hundred and twelve. A tie!
Then Mrs. Pickles walked up. She opened her purse. One dollar. All for Biscuit.
But the screen said: six hundred and twenty-five dollars. Exactly enough to fix the school roof. My promise came true. I just wasn't the Mayor.
And yes, this part is real. A town in Kentucky has had dog mayors since nineteen ninety-eight. One dollar a vote.
Biscuit's first job as Mayor? Peeing on my poster. Again.
Who gets your vote? The kid, or the dog?
